title: Visual pigments in a palaeognath bird, the emu Dromaius novaehollandiae: implications for spectral sensitivity and the origin of ultraviolet vision
note: Full text read (control-room oa job run 1), published version (PubMed Central). The emu's own pigment peaks are 367 (UVS), 453, 502 and 562 nm for single cones, 562-563 nm for double cones and 501 nm for rods; the abstract prints the UVS peak as 376 nm, while the Results, Fig. 1 and the SWS1 section give 367 nm. The per-cell data (Table S2) are supplementary and were not in the text read.
